site_name: Meta Fort Worth Data Center (AllianceTexas, 4500 Like Way)
load_basis: no MW figure published by Meta; campus is 2.5 million sq ft on 170 acres across five build phases (Fort Worth Report), full campus completed 2023 (DPR)
notes: Serving utility NOT found after 4 searches and direct fetches of Meta's info sheet, DPR's project page, Fort Worth Report, Data Center Knowledge, Dallas Innovates and CommercialSearch. None names the delivery utility; they describe only a dedicated on-site substation and a 200 MW Clay County wind supply arranged with Citigroup Energy, Alterra and Starwood. Our Denton County Elec Coop (CoServ) assignment is unverified; Oncor and Tri-County Electric Coop are both plausible and should be checked against PUCT service-area records or a Brazos/Oncor substation filing. Directory sites list Oncor but are not citable. Energized year: first building operational 2017 (Fort Worth Report: 'the first was operational by 2017'; DPR: first phase operational in 2017), so our 2021 (from a 2020 generator permit for a later phase) is four years late. Our 658.6 MW has no public counterpart and should be treated as generator nameplate for the whole campus, not load.

site_name: QTS Irving campus DC1/DC2 (6431 Longhorn Dr)
load_basis: operator page: '165 MW+ critical campus capacity' across six buildings (DC1-DC6 on Longhorn Dr); not stated how much is built as of 2025. Bisnow 2014: 'QTS owned on-site 140MVA dual-fed substation'
notes: Serving utility NOT confirmed from an acceptable source. Directory sites list Oncor as power provider (not citable), and QTS's own campus page names no utility. Our Farmers Electric Coop assignment was a flagged fallback and is almost certainly wrong for Irving, but I found no citable source to replace it; Oncor is the lead to confirm. Energized year: Bisnow, 16 Oct 2014, reports the grand opening 'yesterday' of the converted semiconductor plant at 6431 Longhorn Dr, so our 2022 (from a 2021 generator permit, likely a later building) is eight years late. The 165 MW+ figure is campus-wide critical capacity per the operator and is recorded as planned buildout; DC6 was still under construction through 2025 per directory listings. Note the operator's site now redirects from qtsdatacenters.com to q.com.

site_name: Edged Atlanta (ATL01, former Tilford Yard; operator address 1800 Thomas St NW)
load_basis: built critical capacity of the first building (ATL01-1), online August 2024; second building (100 MW) was still under construction in January 2025 and its status at end-2025 was not confirmed
notes: Utility: the operator's grand-opening release and Data Center Frontier both call Georgia Power the 'local utility provider' (it attended the opening), and DCF reports dual utility feeds from two dedicated substations at opposite ends of the campus. A DatacenterDynamics article reportedly says power is 'sourced from Georgia Power' but returned 403 and was not read, hence medium rather than high. Arrangement assumed ordinary retail; no special contract found. Energized: release dated 22 Aug 2024 says the first building is 'now online, delivering 27 MW'. Campus plan is three buildings totalling 168 MW (27 + 100 + 41) per Southern Company/PowerSecure, Jan 2025. Our 189.8 MW exceeds the full planned campus and is far above the 27 MW built at opening. Worklist address (1968 Marietta Rd NW) and operator address (1800 Thomas St NW) are the same Tilford Yard site.

site_name: Amazon CMH070 campus (2675 Newton Ct, New Albany International Business Park area)
load_basis: no public MW figure found for this campus; capacities are redacted in the PUCO filing
notes: Utility: the public (redacted) joint application of Amazon Data Services and Ohio Power Company in PUCO Case No. 23-0858-EL-AEC states that ADS 'operates [redacted] data centers in AEP Ohio's territory across [redacted] data center campuses in Hilliard, Dublin, and New Albany, Ohio', and that a 2018 economic development arrangement (Case No. 17-1827-EL-AEC) supports ADS data centers in the greater Columbus region. That supports AEP Ohio and a special-contract arrangement for Amazon's New Albany campuses generally, but the filing does not name this specific campus or address, and I did not confirm the outcome of the 2023 case; hence medium. The copy read is hosted by a TV station; the docket itself is on the PUCO DIS site. Licking Rural Electric (The Energy Cooperative) remains the alternative and was not ruled out by a site-specific document. Energized year not found; our 2023 is unverified. No rate or price information was collected.

site_name: Aligned PHX-07 (8785 N Reems Rd, Waddell/Glendale)
load_basis: no operator MW figure for PHX-07; operator page lists only the address and design features. PHX-13 on the Glendale campus is 72 MW (under construction, 2025)
notes: Utility: ConstructConnect (19 May 2025) reports 'Arizona Public Service (APS) will build a new 230 kV transmission line to meet the campus's substantial energy requirements' for Aligned's 100-acre Glendale campus where PHX-13 is being built. The article does not mention PHX-07 or Reems Rd; that PHX-07 sits on the same campus comes from directory listings only, so the link to this exact address is partly inferred (medium). Aligned's own page confirms PHX-07 is at 8785 N Reems Rd, Waddell and names no utility. The other mapped candidates are irrigation and tribal districts with no evident connection. Energized year: a 2025 DatacenterDynamics article reportedly said PHX-07 was due to go live later in 2025, but the page returned 403 and I saw it only as a search-result summary of a forward-looking statement; treat 2025 as unconfirmed. Arrangement assumed retail; no special contract found. Our 134.4 MW is unverified.

site_name: CyrusOne Aurora I / CHI1 (2905 Diehl Rd; former CME Group data center)
load_basis: operator page gives '114 MW' total IT capacity and 450,000 sq ft of technical space for the whole Aurora campus (CHI1, CHI2, CHI3), including the newer Bilter Rd build; no figure for 2905 Diehl Rd alone
notes: Utility is an INFERENCE, not a finding. No source names the utility for 2905 Diehl Rd. Patch (3 Oct 2024) and CyrusOne's own release (13 Sep 2024, quoting ComEd's CEO) say CyrusOne's second Aurora campus on Bilter Rd will be 'powered by ComEd', and Patch notes 'Its first is located at 2905 Diehl Road'. The site is inside the City of Aurora, and Naperville's municipal electric utility serves Naperville, so our City of Naperville assignment (smallest polygon) looks like a boundary artifact; ComEd is the only other mapped candidate. Confirm with a ComEd or City of Naperville service-area record before relying on it. Directory listings describe a wholly-owned on-site substation. Energized year not found from an acceptable source: CyrusOne says it has 'been in Aurora since 2016' (when it bought the building), and the Chicago Tribune says CME's data hub operates in it; directories date the original CME build to 2009, which would make our 2018 (from a 2017 generator permit, probably the CHI2 expansion) too late. Our 99.3 MW is below the 114 MW campus IT figure but not comparable building-for-building.

site_name: Amazon (AWS) Hermiston campus, E Penney Ave
load_basis: no public MW figure found from an acceptable source
notes: Utility: City of Hermiston Planning Commission minutes, 10 May 2023, minor partition for Amazon Data Services at 994 E Penney Ave: 'The proposed partition creates two lots, one for the data center and one for a substation that will service the data center. Umatilla Electric Cooperative (UEC) plans to acquire the lot with the substation.' Two commissioners declared UEC ties. Amazon's own April 2023 post calls UEC 'the electric cooperative serving AWS in Umatilla and Morrow Counties' (https://www.aboutamazon.com/news/aws/data-center-oregon-renewable-energy). The worklist address is 972 E Penney Ave; the record is for the adjoining 994/908 E Penney Ave Amazon parcels, which I take to be the same campus. Our BPA assignment is wrong as the retail deliverer (BPA is the federal wholesale/transmission agency); City of Hermiston (Hermiston Energy Services) is not the provider either. Arrangement: marked special_contract because Amazon and UEC announced in 2023 that Amazon would select the electricity supply for its data centers through UEC rather than take the co-op's standard supply; I did not see the contract itself, so treat the arrangement label as medium confidence. Energized year not found: the partition was at preliminary-plat stage in May 2023, so first operation was 2024 or later, but no acceptable source dates it.

site_name: Vantage San Antonio TX2 campus, building TX21 (5207 Rogers Rd)
load_basis: Texas TDLR project record title 'Vantage Data Centers TX21 Core and Shell +16MW Fit-Out' (360,000 sq ft, estimated completion 6/1/2025); first-phase fit-out, not a metered load. San Antonio Current (Jul 2026) describes the site as a '32-megawatt operation'
notes: Our CPS Energy assignment is NOT confirmed and may be wrong in kind. No source names CPS Energy as serving this site. Instead, Deceleration (8 Jun 2026) reports a 150 MW gas power plant arranged on the same site and quotes an opposing attorney: 'Vantage cannot obtain power for the data center from the utility'; San Antonio Current (13 Jul 2026) reports 'The 32-megawatt operation will be powered by its own gas power plant and 65 diesel backup generators, Vantage officials said'; News4 (12 Aug 2026) says the Rogers Rd and Omicron Dr sites 'are constructing their own natural gas power plants on-site'. Deceleration adds it is 'unclear if the power plant at the Rogers Road location is already operational'. So the arrangement is recorded as behind_the_meter at low confidence; whether the part of TX21 operating in 2025 took grid service from CPS Energy in the interim is unknown and is the key thing to resolve (TCEQ permit file or CPS Energy). Energized year: TDLR lists estimated completion 1 Jun 2025 and 2026 reporting says the building is 'already operating, at least partially'; first operation in 2025 is likely but not directly documented. Our 82.4 MW is far above the 16 MW first fit-out and the 32 MW described by the operator. A second building (TX22) is under construction for 2027.

site_name: Google Red Oak data center campus
load_basis: no MW figure from an acceptable source; Google has published only the 2023 investment announcement
notes: Utility is weakly supported. Switchgear Magazine (27 Mar 2026) reports that a new Oncor 765/345 kV substation in Ellis County will 'aggregate loads for major customers, including data centres in the Ellis County corridor ... such as Databank, Compass, Google, Amazon, Skybox, Stack and QTS'. That names Oncor as serving Google load in Ellis County (Google has both Midlothian and Red Oak there) but concerns a future substation and does not name the Red Oak campus's current feed, so confidence is low. It does cut against our HILCO Electric Coop assignment (smallest polygon); no source mentions HILCO, Navarro County EC or United. In Oncor's territory retail supply would come through a competitive retailer or direct arrangement, which was not identified. Energized year: Google's Texas page lists Red Oak as one of its two Texas data center locations but gives no opening date (https://datacenters.google/locations/texas/); Fox 4 (14 Nov 2025) says 'another AI facility opened its doors in Red Oak this week' without naming the operator, and a local market site says Google Red Oak has been 'Operational since November 2025' without a citation. 2025 agrees with our guess but is low confidence. Directory figures for building capacity were not used.

site_name: Digital Realty ORD12 (9333 Grand Ave, Franklin Park campus 'Digital Chicago')
load_basis: no building-level MW published; operator lists ORD12 at 110,000 sq ft. 2012 campus plan was twenty 1.125 MW PODs, '32.6 megawatts of IT load', across the three Grand Ave buildings
notes: Utility: Data Center Knowledge (6 Jun 2012): 'Primary electrical service for Digital Chicago will be provided by Commonwealth Edison Company.' ComEd and Digital Realty also announced a new substation serving the Franklin Park campus on 7 Nov 2022 (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20221107005870/en; page returned 403, headline only). Matches our assignment. Energized year: the 2012 article says the first phase (six PODs) 'is expected to be delivered and operational by mid-2013'; that is a forward-looking date consistent with the 2013 generator permit, so 2013 at medium confidence versus our 2014. planned_full_buildout_mw is the 2012 campus-wide IT plan (9333, 9355 and 9377 Grand Ave together), not this building alone; later figures quoted in search results (44.4 MW IT, 60 MW ComEd service) could not be traced to a readable primary document and were not used. Our 69.9 MW looks like generator nameplate for the campus, not IT load of one 110,000 sq ft building.

site_name: Amazon data center, AmeriPlex at the Port (6350 Prairie School Dr, Portage)
load_basis: no MW figure published; project described as an $87 million facility ($35 million building, $52 million IT equipment)
notes: Utility is an INFERENCE, not a finding. No source names the utility for the Portage site. NIPSCO is the only mapped utility here, and Amazon's 24 Nov 2025 Northern Indiana announcement describes a framework with NIPSCO and its subsidiary NIPSCO Generation LLC 'to power Amazon data centers', but that page does not mention Portage and concerns the much larger new campuses (IURC special-contract docket reported as Cause No. 46322). Do not assume the Portage facility is under that special contract; arrangement left unknown. Inside Indiana Business (20 Dec 2023) confirms Amazon is building an $87 million data center in AmeriPlex at the Port and says 'A timeline for the facility's opening was not provided', so the energized year is not established; our 2024 is unverified. The investment size suggests a small facility, and our 65.2 MW may overstate it considerably. No rate or price information was collected.
